newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-TOP SEED DONG PULLS OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-TOP SEED DONG PULLS OUT OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Top seed Dong Jiong of China scratched from the world badminton championships on Thursday, handing a quarter-final slot to Denmark's Thomas Stuer-Lauridsen.
The departure of the All England champion had been foreshadowed when coach Li Mao disclosed earlier in the day that the player had a fever.

It was a lucky break for Stuer-Lauridsen and he was joined in the last eight soon afterwards by compatriot Peter Rasmussen who scored a surprise win 15-8 8-15 15-1 success over Indonesia's Indra Wijaya, seeded four.

But Wijaya's fellow countryman Heryanto Arbi, the defending champion who has dropped to 12 in the seedings following a back injury, maintained his hopes of retaining the title with a 15-12 15-8 win over the number six seed from Malaysia, Ong Ewe Hock.
Rasmussen needed three games to overcome Wijaya, but eventually ran out a comfortable winner to earn a last eight clash with South Korea's Park Sung-woo.

"Wijaya played very well in the second game, and I became too predictable," said the 22-year-old Rasmussen. "But during the five-minute break my coach, Steen Pedersen, told me to play more cross-court shots, and use the short serve.
"If you lift the shuttle against Wijaya, he is very dangerous. I've been thinking about these world championships for a long time, and it's wonderful to have made it through to the quarter-finals."
Stuer-Lauridsen, the number 10 seed, was relieved to have avoided a clash with the world number one, Dong.
"I've had to pull out myself several times in the past through illness or injury, so this is my turn to get lucky," said the Dane, who now meets Arbi for a place in the semifinals.
In the women's event, China's world number one, Ye Zhaoying, had no trouble reaching the quarter-finals.
She needed under 15 minutes to beat Indonesia's Cindana 11-4 11-1.
